scenes.title: Key ideas
items: A CDP (collateralised debt position) lets you lock collateral and mint a stablecoin…
The stablecoin holds its peg through over-collateralisation, liquidations, interest…
Compared with borrowing from a lending pool
scenes.vo: First, A C.D.P. (collateralised debt position) lets you lock collateral and mint a stablecoin against it. You owe the stablecoin back, plus a stability fee (interest). Next, Minimum collateral ratio (for example 150%): below it, the position is liquidated. Then, the stablecoin holds its peg through over-collateralisation, liquidations, interest rates and often a peg stability module (P.S.M.) that swaps it 1:1 (minus a small fee) with other stablecoins. Also, Compared with borrowing from a lending pool: you create new money rather than borrow someone's deposit; rates are set by governance, not utilisation. And finally, Uses: liquidity without selling (Module 12.3), funding a liquidity ladder, or a yield-covered credit line (strategy #25).

scenes.title: Worked example
steps: 10 ETH at $3,000 ($30,000) with a 150% minimum ratio
Operators treat the maximum as a cliff, not a target.
scenes.vo: Let's work an example, step by step. 10 ETH at $3,000 ($30,000) with a 150% minimum ratio: you could mint up to $20,000. Mint $10,000 instead: the calculator to ratio 300%, liquidation at $1,500 (minus 50%), stability fee $600 a year. Operators treat the maximum as a cliff, not a target.

scenes.title: Checklist
items: Collateral ratio target (e.g. ≥ 250%) and action levels written
Stability fee vs alternatives (lending-pool borrow rates) compared
Peg mechanism (PSM, rates) understood, and my exit if the stablecoin depegs
scenes.vo: Here's your checklist. Do it now, for real. First, Collateral ratio target (for example at least 250%) and action levels written. Next, Stability fee versus alternatives (lending-pool borrow rates) compared. And finally, Peg mechanism (P.S.M., rates) understood, and my exit if the stablecoin depegs.

scenes.q: What do you owe on a CDP?
scenes.a: The minted stablecoin plus the accrued stability fee.
